Budanov said the proposal for a temporary halt to airstrikes and frontline combat was communicated directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin. While noting the ongoing Russian drone attacks, Budanov speculated that Moscow would not strike Kyiv

US Envoys Witkoff and Kushner Arrive in Moscow for Talks — US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived at Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport on Saturday, Sept. 5. Russian state media published footage of a motorcade receiving the delegation, while flight tracking data showed their Boeing C-32A aircraft traveling from Miami via Helsinki. The envoys are expected to hold talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow before traveling to Kyiv on Sunday, Sept. 6, to meet with President Vol

Kyiv Airports Struck in Response to US Diplomacy, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sept. 5 that Russian forces conducted “demonstrative” overnight drone strikes on airports in Kyiv and Boryspil. Zelensky linked the attacks to preparations for the upcoming arrival of US peace envoys, characterizing the use of “Shahed” drones as a direct response to American diplomacy. He stated Ukraine would adjust its operations regarding Russian airspace next week in response.

Expert Downplays US Envoys’ Diplomatic Mission — Daniel Hamilton, president of the Transatlantic Leadership Network, has expressed that the upcoming visit by US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Kyiv and Moscow is unlikely to produce a diplomatic breakthrough. Hamilton noted that Russian President Vladimir Putin is increasing pressure on Ukraine and expanding sabotage operations across Europe. He dismissed US President Donald Trump’s proposal for European reimbursement of military

Combat Continues as Russia Rejects Ceasefire — The Armed Forces of Ukraine confirmed on Saturday, Sept. 5, that combat operations will continue after Russia rejected a proposed mutual ceasefire for Sept. 5-9. The General Staff stated a unilateral pause would endanger personnel, though strikes at operational depth have been temporarily restricted. The Russian Defense Ministry confirmed its refusal by conducting overnight combined strikes, including a ballistic missile attack on an industrial faci

Kherson Region Drone Attacks Injure 6 Civilians — Russian forces launched a series of drone strikes across the city of Kherson and the village of Molodizhne on Saturday morning, Sept. 5, injuring six civilians. The regional attacks occurred alongside a wider overnight aerial campaign across Ukraine, which included a deadly ballistic missile strike on an industrial enterprise in Kamianske that killed five people, and consecutive drone strikes on a Mykolaiv shopping center that injured two.

NB8 Nations Secure $1B for Ukraine’s Winter Energy Needs — First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal announced that the Nordic-Baltic Eight (NB8) nations will work to attract additional financial and technical support for Ukraine’s energy grid ahead of the winter. Shmyhal noted that the NB8 has already allocated at least €918 million ($1 billion) in 2026 for energy infrastructure protection and recovery, adding that Ukraine is ready to share its expertise in defending against
The Skeleton Putin Needs — Why Russia is mobilizing a fourteenth-century prince for the war against Ukraine.

Ukrainian Refugees Leave Poland Amid Rising Tensions — Ukrainian refugees are increasingly leaving Poland for other European nations, primarily Germany and the Czech Republic, according to updated Eurostat data. The number of Ukrainians with temporary protection in Poland fell by 14,400 over June and July to approximately 953,000, while Germany’s total reached nearly 1.3 million. The migration coincides with a 30% year-over-year increase in hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland during the fir

Zelensky Secures Diplomatic Backing for Black Sea Grain Routes — President Volodymyr Zelensky stated on Sept. 4 that diplomatic decisions are being prepared to secure Black Sea food transportation. Addressing the threat of a global food crisis, Zelensky confirmed ongoing talks regarding export corridors with Egypt, Turkey, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. The diplomatic push coincides with Ukraine’s efforts to establish alternative export routes following intensified Russian strikes on Odesa port infr

Kremlin Downplays Hopes for Breakthrough in US Envoys’ Visit — The Kremlin views the chances of a diplomatic breakthrough during the upcoming visit of US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as “extremely low”. Sources indicate Russian President Vladimir Putin is hardening his demands, insisting on the full transfer of the Donetsk region to Russian control due to perceived battlefield advantages.

Russian Strikes Kill 5 in Kamianske, Injure 2 in Mykolaiv — A Russian ballistic missile struck an industrial enterprise in Kamianske on Sept. 5, killing five people and injuring five others, while jet-powered drones hit an Epicenter shopping center in Mykolaiv, injuring two in a double-tap attack. The strikes occurred following a Russian attack on a residential building in Boryspil on Friday.

Norway Ship Seizure Raises Stakes as Moscow Fears Wider Russian Asset Confiscations — Norway’s seizure of a Russian vessel for Ukraine’s Naftogaz has sharpened concerns in Moscow that more Russian state assets abroad could be targeted to satisfy Ukrainian compensation claims.

Russian Agent Near SBU HQ May Have Guided Shahed Strike, Expert Says — Presidential adviser Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov believes a Russian operative may have activated a portable internet-linked radio repeater within 5 kilometers of the SBU headquarters to guide the Shahed that struck the building.

Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Will Russia Honor Zelensky’s Proposed Truce for US Envoys? — Zelensky offered a reciprocal pause in air strikes during the visit of Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, as fresh Russian attacks raise doubts over Moscow’s intentions.
Russian Attack Sets Nine-Story Residential Building Ablaze in Boryspil — A Russian attack damaged a nine-story apartment building in Boryspil, Kyiv region, setting the roof and one apartment on fire.

Memorial Chief Warns Russia Will Jail More People, Send Them to Front Line in Ukraine After Elections — Memorial executive director Elena Zhemkova warned that political repression in Russia could sharply intensify after September’s elections, with more people imprisoned and sent to fight in Ukraine.

Zelensky Approves Response Plans After Russian Strikes: ‘We Will Choose the Right Time’ — Zelensky said he approved proposals from Ukraine’s security service and military to answer Russian strikes, promising Moscow a response “at the right time.”

Ukraine’s Anti-Graft Agencies Search Prosecutor General’s Office, Odesa Governor — Ukrainian anti-corruption investigators launched a major operation at the Prosecutor General’s Office, with searches reported at premises linked to senior officials. The Prosecutor General’s Office denied that Ruslan Kravchenko himself was searched.

Trump Confirms Envoys’ Visit to Kyiv, Says ‘Personality Issues’ Caused Stalled Diplomacy — US President Donald Trump confirmed that senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are carrying a proposal to end the war, while blaming stalled diplomacy on personal animosity between President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin. However, some sources suggest Russia may be pressuring the envoys to cancel their Kyiv visit.

Rescuers Help Kharkiv Families Flee Frontline Danger — Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (SES) evacuates residents from frontline communities, including in the Kharkiv region, as Russian strikes intensify. Rescuers and psychologists provide both physical and emotional support as civilian casualties reach record levels across Ukraine.

Criminal Network Led by Prosecutor General’s Office Authority Exposed by NABU, SAPO — Following the announcement of a new probe dubbed “Forrest Gump” in August, Ukraine’s anti-graft agencies – NABU and SAPO – stepped up their efforts to target criminal organizations involving current and former Ukrainian senior officials. On Friday, the head of the Cyber Department at the Prosecutor General’s Office, Serhii Kropyva, was detained for involvement in a network of fraudulent call centers and money-l

Zelensky Confirms US Envoys Will Visit Kyiv on Sunday, After Visiting Moscow — President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed a Sunday meeting in Kyiv with senior US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, following their scheduled visit to Moscow on the same weekend. According to Zelensky, Ukraine will ensure safe passage through Russian airspace for the delegation.

Croatian Court Delays Ukrainian Nord Stream Suspect’s Extradition Hearing Amid New Charges — A county court in Pula, Croatia, postponed the extradition hearing for Ukrainian national Volodymyr Zhuravlev scheduled for Friday, Sept. 4, as Germany updated the European arrest warrant with a classification of a “war crime.” This was announced by the law firm representing Zhuravlev, “Katerynchuk, Moor and Partners.”

China Lures Russia’s Far East Firms With Cheap 3% Loans — Chinese industrial and technology parks are attracting companies from Russia’s Far East with lower taxes, loans carrying 3% interest and capital investment grants. A Russian business leader said several firms had already registered in China, although consultants reported no significant wave of relocations.

Russia Attacks Teva Pharmaceutical Company and World Health Organization Warehouse in Ukraine — Russian drone assault hit the Ukrainian facilities of Teva Pharmaceuticals and a primary World Health Organization warehouse on Sept. 3. As one of the largest international drugmakers in Ukraine, Teva is urgently assessing the damage to prevent supply chain disruptions and protect patient access to essential medicines.

Ukraine Reveals Moscow Invite for Possible Putin Meeting — Russian negotiators unexpectedly invited a Ukrainian delegation to continue peace talks in Moscow after a February meeting in Geneva, potentially opening the way for talks with Vladimir Putin. Presidential Office head Kyrylo Budanov said the visit never materialized but expects US-mediated negotiations to resume by late September.

Colombian Volunteers Fighting for Ukraine Capture Ground, Russian Defenses in Assault — A Ukrainian unit – mostly of Colombian and Brazilian volunteers – captured Russian positions in the northeast, adding 4 sq. km to gains from a mini-offensive launched last week.

Ukraine, Poland Explore Joint World Cup Bid for 2040s — Ukraine and Poland are exploring a joint bid to host the men’s FIFA World Cup, building on their successful partnership during Euro 2012. No formal proposal has been submitted, but Ukrainian officials say preparations must begin now for a possible tournament in the 2040s.

Thousands Arrive in Wartime Ukraine for One of the World’s Largest Jewish Pilgrimages — Around 40,000 pilgrims are expected to celebrate Rosh Hashanah in Uman from Sept. 11-13. The city will impose special restrictions on entry, exit and movement.

Witkoff-Kushner: Your Visit to a Nation Under Fire Is Unwelcome, Unless… — Kyiv is not a trading floor, and the liberty of millions of Ukrainians is not a commodity to be bartered away after consulting the Kremlin’s preferences.

Russian Drone Strikes SBU Headquarters in Central Kyiv, Targets Chief’s Office — A Russian drone struck the central Kyiv headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service and was aimed at chief Oleksandr Poklad’s office, President Zelensky said. He ordered a “tangible” response to the attack, which occurred near the historic St. Sophia Cathedral.

Ukraine Could Grant Wartime Presidents Lifetime Protection Under New Bill — Ukrainian lawmakers have introduced a bill that would grant lifetime state protection to presidents who served during wartime and their families, except when the president was removed through impeachment. Former members of the supreme command staff and the National Security and Defense Council could receive protection for 10 years after leaving office.

Kyiv Proposes Turning Metrohrad Mall Into Underground Parking — Kyiv authorities have proposed turning 17,000 square meters (4 acres) of the Metrohrad mall in central Kyiv into underground parking spaces and a shelter, amid criticism over inadequate parking and shelter space. However, officials also acknowledge the complexity of the whole idea.

Unscathed by Russian Strikes, Ukraine Region Offers Wartime Respite — Zakarpattia has largely escaped the destruction seen elsewhere in Ukraine, offering residents and displaced Ukrainians a rare sense of normality. But as a veteran’s story shows, even this relatively peaceful western region cannot escape the emotional weight of Russia’s war.

Ukraine Unveils Highest-Denomination Banknote Featuring Vasyl Stus — Ukraine’s central bank introduced the country’s new highest-denomination banknote on Sept. 4. The note features Vasyl Stus and marks two pivotal events in the dissident poet’s life that occurred on the same date.

Ukraine Names Ivan Fedorov Head of Recovery Agency — Ukraine’s government has appointed Ivan Fedorov, the outgoing head of the Zaporizhzhia regional administration and former mayor of occupied Melitopol, to lead the State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development. He replaces Serhiy Sukhomlyn and will oversee the protection and rebuilding of infrastructure repeatedly targeted by Russia.

No Evidence of FPV Drones Launched From Jet-Powered Shaheds in Kyiv, Expert Says — Three days of searches found no evidence that Russia used jet-powered Shaheds to carry FPV drones over Kyiv. Ukrainian expert Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov says the technology exists but is used with conventional Shaheds, whose lower speed makes carrying FPVs possible.

Bessent Points Finger at Ukraine for Energy Price Surge — US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said after the G20 that Ukraine is “creating upward price pressure” by hitting Russian refineries before mentioning the war in Iran in passing – but think tank data suggests that Russia’s overall export volumes stayed mostly flat in recent months despite the attacks, as losses in refined volumes were made up for by crude, albeit with lower revenues.

Witkoff, Kushner Rumored to Visit Moscow Before Kyiv on Sept. 5-6 — Trump’s envoys Kushner and Witkoff are reportedly set to visit Moscow before Kyiv to promote trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US on Sept. 5-6. A Russian drone reportedly struck two Soviet-era planes at Zhulyany Airport, but claims about the envoys’ planned flight remain unconfirmed.

Russian Drone Hits Kyiv Site as Claims Emerge of Aircraft Strike Ahead of US Envoys’ Visit — A fire broke out at a non-residential site in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district during a Russian drone attack, but authorities did not identify the facility affected. Unverified reports pointed to either a Nova Poshta hub or an aircraft at Zhulyany Airport, while MP Oleksiy Goncharenko linked the latter claim to tentative travel plans for US envoys.

Ukraine’s Intel Strikes Russian Bastion Missile System in Crimea — Ukraine’s military intelligence said Group 13 struck a Russian Bastion system used to launch Zircon and Oniks missiles against Ukraine. The unit also reportedly destroyed or damaged two fuel trucks and a Russian command-and-staff vehicle.

52% Back Ukraine Arms, 42% Say Germany Has Gone Too Far, Deutschland Poll Finds — A majority of Germans still support arms deliveries to Ukraine, though 42% say Berlin is going too far. Meanwhile, 56% see Russia as a major threat to Germany, with older voters particularly concerned.

Germany Records 165 Suspected Sabotage Cases This Year — German authorities registered more than 165 suspected sabotage cases nationwide through the end of August, according to a confidential police assessment. The report also listed 747 suspicious drone incidents involving 1,068 aircraft over critical infrastructure, military sites, and defense companies. Investigators recorded 112 espionage-related crimes and opened 24 espionage cases.

Meloni Breaks Italy’s Post-War Political Record — Giorgia Meloni’s government has become Italy’s longest-serving administration since Mussolini, marking a rare period of political stability. However, her initial political momentum has faded. Meloni now faces rising living costs, coalition disputes over defence, tensions with Donald Trump, and pressure from Italy’s nationalist right as she prepares for the 2027 election.

Ukraine to Introduce Two-Level Air Raid Alert System as Drone Attacks Disrupt Daily Life — Ukraine is overhauling its air raid alert system as relentless Russian drone attacks disrupt daily life. A new two-tier system will distinguish drone threats from missile and ballistic attacks, while Kyiv is urged to keep the metro running and shorten curfew hours.

Russian Conscripts Increasingly Blocked From Leaving Country Amid Mobilization Fears — Russian conscripts are increasingly being blocked from leaving the country, even as Putin dismisses fresh mobilization reports as an “information attack.” Dozens have been stopped at Russian and Belarusian borders amid growing speculation that Moscow is preparing for another mass call-up.

Russia Changes Strategy: Non-Stop Alerts in Kyiv — Russia has shifted its attacks on Kyiv to prolonged drone bombardments, aiming to exhaust Ukraine’s air defences and disrupt civilian life. Ukrainian voices stress resilience, honest government communication, and societal unity. Meanwhile, attacks on warehouses, ports and shipping threaten Ukraine’s agriculture and economy, making resilient logistics and supply infrastructure crucial for surviving the coming winter.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Sochi Oil Depot, Air Defense Systems as Moscow Faces Third Night of Flight Disruptions — Ukrainian drones attacked Sochi overnight, setting fire to a Rosneft oil depot and reportedly hitting Russian S-300/S-400 air defenses. A defense plant in Bashkortostan was also targeted, while 35 drones were reportedly shot down near Moscow, disrupting flights for a third consecutive night.

Kernel Secures €100 Million in Financing for 94.5 MW Wind Power Plant — Ukrainian agricultural company Kernel signed a €100 million loan agreement with Denmark’s Export and Investment Fund (EIFO) to finance its first wind energy project, featuring 21 Vestas turbines and industrial energy storage systems in central Ukraine.

Russian Strike on Odesa Kills 1, Injures at Least 3 — Russia struck Odesa early Friday, killing one person and injuring at least three as residential buildings and vehicles were damaged.

Fact-Checking Putin: Is Russia Exporting More Crude by Choice or Out of Options? — Putin argued that crude exports make economic sense as oil prices rise, but Russia’s fuel shortages, imports and damaged refineries tell a different story.

Russian Drone Strike Sets Zaporizhzhia Apartment Building Ablaze — A Russian drone struck a residential building in Zaporizhzhia overnight, setting apartments on fire as authorities assessed casualties and damage.

All 4 Moscow Airports Hit by Flight Delays, Cancellations for Third Night — A third night of drone alerts hit Moscow as airport restrictions spread across Russia, forcing cancellations, delays and diversions far beyond the capital.

Russia Demands ‘Immediate Release’ of Ship Seized by Norway Over Naftogaz Claim — The Russian vessel remains detained in Svalbard as Naftogaz seeks to enforce a $4.2 billion arbitration award over assets seized in Crimea.

Coca-Cola Production Facility in Kyiv Region Confirms Russian Drone Damage — Russian forces struck a Coca-Cola production facility in Brovary, Kyiv region on Thursday, Sept. 3. In a comment to RBC-Ukraine, the company confirmed the drone attack and said no employees were injured. Meanwhile, President Volodymyr Zelensky called the strike a signal to the US.

Ukraine Shortens Kyiv’s Curfew as Cabinet Adjusts to Changing Russian Air Attack Tactics — According to Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, the Cabinet of Ministers approved new measures on Thursday, Sept. 3, including shortened curfew hours and a new two-tier yellow and red air alert system, as Ukraine adapts to Russia’s evolving aerial attack tactics.

Zelensky Orders Dismissal of SBU, HUR Deputy Chiefs Over Shootout in Kyiv — A shootout between personnel from the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and Ukraine’s Military Intelligence (HUR) took place in Kyiv on Wednesday, Sept. 2, linked to a case reportedly involving the deputy commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps (RDK). Later that day, President Volodymyr Zelensky called the incident “absolutely disgraceful” and demanded accountability. On Thursday, Sept. 3, Zelensky announced the dismiss

8.1 Million Passengers Traveled By Ukrainian Railways This Summer — Ukrainian state railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia transported 8.14 million passengers during the summer of 2026, maintaining a multi-year growth trend. This steady increase comes despite severe operational challenges, including a shrinking railcar fleet and relentless Russian military strikes.

Zelensky Confirms US Envoys’ Planned Diplomatic Visit to Kyiv and Moscow — President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Thursday, Sept. 3 that US special presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner plan on visiting both Moscow and Kyiv in the upcoming days, amid stalled diplomacy between Ukraine and Russia.

Zelensky Discusses Support for Ukraine With Peru’s President Fujimori — President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori on Thursday, Sept. 3, for the first time since her inauguration in late July. He thanked her for her country’s continued condemnation of Russia’s invasion, and announced that the two also discussed bilateral trade and drone technologies.

India’s Double Game with Russia: Peace Rhetoric vs Record Oil Trade — While Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly urges Russian leader Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine, New Delhi is silently deepening its strategic and economic ties with Moscow. In this video, we break down the changing equation of India-Russia relations: from record-breaking Russian crude oil imports (exceeding 2.6 million barrels per day) to India supplying refined gasoline back to Russia, trade imbalances, and

13 Wounded, Including 1 Child, in Russian Strikes on Kyiv — Russian forces struck Kyiv, including the wider region, on Thursday, Sept. 3, launching more than 163 drones overnight. One civilian was injured in the morning attacks, while the number of casualties in Kyiv rose to 13 later in the evening.

Russian House Shutdown: Decisive Move or Convenient Timing? — Berlin’s Russian House is the largest of a worldwide network operated by sanctioned Kremlin agency Rossotrudnichestvo. Critics accuse it of spreading propaganda, supporting Russian influence operations and using litigation to intimidate journalists. Germany has now announced its closure, but it is using an ordinary non-renewal clause that will not take effect until June 2027.

Russian Strike Injures 3, Damages Kyiv Apartment Block During Tuesday’s Barrage — A Russian strike damaged the upper floors of a 16-story apartment building in Kyiv’s Podil district, injuring three people. Firefighters rescued seven residents and extinguished a blaze that spread between two floors across an area of 100 square meters (1,076 square feet).

WATCH: Ukraine’s Khartiia Troops Break Through Near Kupyansk, Liberate Another 4 Square Kilometers — The 23rd Assault Regiment R.U.G. liberated another 4 square kilometers (1.5 square miles) in the Kupyansk sector, according to the Khartiia Corps. Ukrainian troops worked alongside the 35th Separate Marine Brigade during parts of the operation.

Ukraine Fast-Tracks Interceptors for Jet-Powered Shahed — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is accelerating development of high-speed interceptor drones to counter Russia’s jet-powered Shaheds. Ukrainian manufacturers have produced prototypes, while officials set deadlines to improve them and involve businesses in air defense production. Zelensky said Ukrainian intel knows Russia’s plans and that unspecified “asymmetric” operations have been approved.

SBU, HUR Offer Conflicting Accounts Over Kyiv Shootout — After a Kyiv shootout on Wednesday, the parties involved now offer conflicting accounts of what happened – the SBU accused an RDK commander (under HUR) of collaboration with Russia’s FSB, whereas the commander named said he was kidnapped, with the Russian plot being a cover-up for his abduction amid accusations of interagency rivalry.

Ukraine Official Says Strategic Attacks in Russia Could End Drone Terror — Counter-Disinformation Center chief Andriy Kovalenko said the only way to halt Russia’s drone attacks is to create comparable pressure at sensitive targets inside Russia. He rejected the idea that air defenses can instantly seal Ukraine’s skies, arguing that the threat must be addressed at its source. Kovalenko said disruptions at Russian airports will increasingly affect the country’s economy and daily life.

‘Watch the News’: Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Teases New Momentum in Peace Talks — Andrii Sybiha said peace efforts could gain “new momentum” as political and diplomatic activity resumes in capitals around the world. He added that progress would be unrealistic without US involvement and urged people to “watch the news.”

Russian General Tied to Okhmatdyt Attack Reportedly Shot — A Russian Telegram channel claimed Maj. Gen. Nikolai Varpakhovich was shot twice outside a home in Saratov Oblast and remained in critical condition. The report has not been independently confirmed. Ukraine’s SBU alleges that Varpakhovich ordered and coordinated the July 2024 missile strike on Kyiv’s Okhmatdyt children’s hospital, which killed two people and injured dozens.

The Last Walk to Maidan: Remembering Eva Reuter — Eva Reuter, a 25-year-old artist-turned-combat medic with Ukraine's Hospitallers battalion, was killed rescuing victims of a Russian strike when attackers hit the scene again in a "double tap." Mourners gathered at Kyiv's St. Michael's Golden-Domed Cathedral before processing to Maidan Nezalezhnosti, where her fiancé, an American serviceman known as "Exile," delivered an emotional tribute to her courage and sacrifice.

Kernel Sells World's First Low-Carbon Sunflower Oil with Climate Premium — Kernel has completed the world's first sale of sunflower oil with a reduced carbon footprint, securing a climate premium from a global corporation after verifying that it cut emissions throughout production.

Fuel, Energy Crisis in Strategic Russia-Occupied Crimea Worsening — Crimea is imposing tighter fuel rationing as Ukrainian strikes disrupt fuel deliveries. Stations will sell only four hours daily, while 20-liter and odd/even license-plate limits remain. Blackouts add to the peninsula’s growing crisis.

Putin Says Ukraine, Russia Must Reach Deal — Putin claims prospects for an agreement between Moscow and Kyiv still exist. A day earlier, he says Russia is refraining from targeting Ukraine’s leadership because it needs officials with whom it can negotiate.

‘We Were Mistaken’: Putin Admits Russia Was Unprepared for Ukrainian Strikes on Oil Refineries — Putin has admitted Russia was “mistaken” in assuming its oil refineries would not be targeted, as Ukrainian drone strikes deepen a fuel crisis that has forced Moscow to turn to foreign gasoline imports.

‘Enemy Did Not Take a Vacation’: Russia Escalates Attacks Across Ukraine, Zelensky Says — President Zelensky said Russia has launched a “new escalation” of its attacks, leaving damage across 13 Ukrainian regions overnight. A drone attack on a residential high-rise in Odesa wounded 17 people, including three children. Zelensky urged Europe to accelerate production of missile and drone defense systems as Russia increasingly deploys jet-powered drones.

Estonia’s Defense Minister Resigns Over Ukraine Ammunition Scandal — Estonian defense minister resigned after a €70 million ammo deal for Ukraine came under scrutiny and prosecutors opened a criminal investigation. Pevkur said he was taking political responsibility, although PM Michal said he saw no personal fault.

Drone Wall Rises: Ukraine Bets on Its Best Corps — A two-week roundup of the Russia-Ukraine war: Ukraine's 1st and 3rd Corps take command of the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk defense, Russia launches a major ballistic missile strike on Kyiv, and Ukrainian forces hit a record 21 Russian oil refineries in August. Plus new weapons debuts, a Banderol missile strike on Pechenihy, and the latest on Russia's fuel and power shortages.

‘No Scenario That Would Require It’: Putin Denies New Russian Mobilization – Again — Putin has again denied that Russia is preparing a new mobilization, calling the reports an “information attack” aimed at disrupting upcoming State Duma elections. His repeated denials come amid growing speculation that Moscow is preparing to expand military recruitment.

Russia to Close Goethe-Institut Branches in Retaliation Against Germany — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Russia would close Goethe-Institut branches across the country in response to Germany’s measures following an explosives-laden drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

Russia Puts TV Propaganda Chiefs Under Guard Amid Threat of Ukrainian Strikes — Russia’s National Guard has stepped up security for senior television executives and prominent presenters, reportedly amid fears they could be targeted by Ukraine.

Tusk Calls Polish Drone Component Plant Fire Sabotage — Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a fire at a WB Electronics plant producing components for unmanned systems was deliberately damaged in an act of sabotage and accused Russia of using cryptocurrency to finance the operation. Authorities have not reached the same conclusion, including a separate blaze at an aviation-components facility in Lublin.

Ukraine’s Drones Reach Moscow’s Doorstep, Hit Homes and Sochi Port — Russian officials say Ukrainian drones hit residential buildings in Moscow Region and caused a fire at a factory, while a separate attack hit the Black Sea port of Sochi.

Ukraine to Help Europe Close Defense Gaps as Russia Threat Grows — Ukraine will join a new European initiative to identify and rapidly address defense gaps, drawing on its battlefield experience against Russia. The effort comes as Europe faces Russian hybrid threats and uncertainty over the future US military role in NATO.

Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Region, Injuring 1 Amid Damaged Warehouses and Buildings — Russian forces attacked Kyiv region on Thursday, Sept. 3, injuring one person and damaging warehouses, an administrative building, a store, and kiosks. Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 163 drones overnight, with 135 shot down or suppressed.

EU Summons Russia Envoys, Eyes Sanctions After Germany Drone ‘Attack’ — EU ministers agreed to advance sanctions against 1,600 Russia-linked individuals and entities after an explosive-laden drone incident at Leipzig airport. They also backed tougher Russian visa restrictions and discussed additional air-defense aid for Ukraine.

Leipzig Case Revives Push for EU Russian Visa Ban — A suspected sabotage plot at Leipzig airport is intensifying EU calls for tougher restrictions on Russian travelers. Ministers also debated the future of the EU’s foreign policy service and negotiations over the bloc’s next long-term budget.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 2, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 2, 2026.

Germany’s Response to Attempted Russian Drone Attack at Leipzig Airport Criticized as Too Weak — Germany attributed the Leipzig/Halle sabotage plot to Russia but kept describing it as a hybrid attack, prompting criticism from Baltic and security officials.

Russian Strike Hits Multi-Story Residential Building in Odesa, Injuring 17, Including 3 Children — A Russian overnight air attack damaged a 21-story residential building in Odesa, injuring 17 people, including 3 children. Apartments on eight floors and several cars were damaged, while emergency and municipal crews continue clearing the aftermath.

Foreign Airlines Begin Suspending Flights to Russia Following Kyiv’s Warning That Its Airspace Is Unsafe — Airlines began canceling flights to Russia after Kyiv warned that expanding drone operations were making the country’s airspace increasingly unsafe for civilian aviation.

Zelensky Says Ukraine, Germany Finalizing Drone Deal as Kyiv Expands Defense Network — Ukraine and Germany are finalizing a bilateral Drone Deal covering joint production and defense cooperation, building on several projects already underway.

Norway Seizes Russian Ship to Enforce $4.2B Naftogaz Award — Norwegian authorities seized a Russian vessel in the Arctic at Naftogaz’s request as the Ukrainian energy company seeks compensation for assets illegally seized by Russia following its 2014 annexation of Crimea.
